title: Intent releases through devbin's core: its driver, kovacs preflight and pre-push build retire
objective:
Intent cuts its releases with devbin's release core instead of its own driver, so one command takes the yes to a brew-installable artefact and no suite or build runs twice for one commit. This is Devbin ST0011's WP12, Intent's line in that thread's per-project remediations. devbin-vc ruled on 2026-10-31, under hv's pen, that this thread in Intent's store is the one place that work is written and claimed; Devbin's WP12 points here.

Concretely:

1. `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release` retires into the core's cut. `release.verbs` gains `cut`; `derived:` carries the schema bless, the lock refresh, `agents sync`, `claude upgrade --apply` and `sync --to-disk`; and a live intentd refuses the cut and its dry run at the core's pre-flight, before anything is stamped. Intent's own checks are declared in `release.gates` rather than made core steps: the bats suite, the cargo gate with 0481's daemon-family re-run, the ST0056 contract and reference checks, the provenance check, and the pair build at the release commit (WP-01).
2. `bin/.devbin/preflight-linux.sh` and `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/preflight.lib` retire into `release.legs`, with kovacs as the leg. `bin/.devbin/cmd/prepush` loses its preflight cover and its clone-and-build, and keeps its frozen-remote refusal (WP-02).
3. `cmd/brew`'s render and publish retire into the built-in formula, and `cmd/macos`'s publish half into the built-in `macos publish`. Intent's own brew smoke stays Intent's and runs as an `after:` command under the cut's yes. `macos prepare` stays as a shadow until the built-in stages more than one app, and writes the stage's commit record, `<stage>/commit` with HEAD's full sha, which the built-in publish requires (WP-03).
4. `tests.yml`, `rust.yml` and `linux-release.yml` fire on `candidate/` refs and not on tags, so every leg, the macOS legs included, is green on the commit that ships before it is tagged. The five hand commands after the tag stop, and `intent/docs/releasing.md` and `.github/workflows/README.md` describe the cut as built (WP-04).
5. Each package is judged and landed on top of the vendor commit that brings the new core into Intent's tree. hv cuts the first release through the core, and that cut's RELEASE seal is the re-read of the 3.2.8 baseline.
context:
**Why.** Devbin's ST0011 diagnosed the release cycle of every project that vendors devbin's release core (hv, 2026-10-31), and found the time goes to repetition rather than to the core's own steps. Intent's 3.2.8 cut on 2026-10-30 took 61m44s from the candidate's commit to the tap. The Ubuntu suite ran three times on GitHub, once on kovacs and once more in the driver on this Mac, and GitHub ran the release commit's workflows twice, once for the push to main and once for the tag. The tap commit went out 2m26s before the shipping commit's macOS CI finished, so no macOS verdict existed for that commit when the formula shipped.

**What was measured, read-only, on 2026-10-31.** dc inventoried every path the remediation names, with its callers, at 7ff46b458, and vc checked the inventory against the tree; it went to devbin-vc at 10:46Z by date -u. vc's baseline of the 3.2.8 cut, read from GitHub, the git reflogs and file times, went at 10:44Z. Intent has no RELEASE seal to read, because the driver writes none.

**devbin-vc's rulings, 2026-10-31, under hv's pen.** This thread is the one place Devbin's WP12 work is written and claimed in Intent; dc claims its packages, and Devbin's WP12 points here. The vendor commit is Devbin's WP09 sweep, committed by vc in Intent's tree, and these packages sit on top of it, so none starts before the sweep, and nothing slow or duplicated is fixed before it either. Of what must survive: 0634's cask sha and the brew smoke go to the built-in formula (Devbin WP08); the candidate is pushed to upstream only, found by its GitHub URL and never as the first remote (Devbin WP02b); the frozen-remote refusal stays in prepush; and 0481's re-run, the contract and reference checks and the provenance check are Intent's own gates, declared in `release.gates`.

**What the core as built changed, 2026-11-10.** dc read the packages again against the vendored devbin 0.1.20 core, vc checked the read in the source, and devbin-vc answered from devbin's main. The core runs no project command before the stamp, so the refusal of a live intentd needs a pre-flight seam. Devbin's next release carries one (devbin 0327), and Intent's first cut through the core waits for that release to be swept in. The same release carries a declared trailer for the release commit's message (devbin 0328), which Intent declares so that the commit keeps its (C) line. hv ruled both that day in devbin-vc's window, as devbin-vc relayed them to vc. The cask's sha256 is filled from the release's sums file, across formula and cask, and that fill stands for issue 0634's check. The brew smoke was never built into the core, so it stays Intent's, as an `after:` command that reports after publication and gates nothing. The pair build is a gate and not a derived step, because a derived step runs before the release commit exists. And the core's formula step refuses a lightweight tag, so Intent's release tags are annotated from this cut on.

**The core's shape** is Devbin ST0011's design.md: the recommended shape (section 5), Intent's line in the per-project remediations (section 7), the leg contract (section 11) and decisions D57 to D68 (section 12), among them D57 (a sealed green for a commit and platform is not run again), D62 (remote legs) and D64 (test workflows fire on `candidate/` and not on tags). This thread does not restate them.

wps.title: The cut runs through devbin's core, and Intent's driver retires
wps.objective: `bin/devbin release` cuts Intent with devbin's core, and `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release` is gone. What the driver does that the core does becomes the core's, and what the core does not do is declared in Intent's config: its own gates in `release.gates` and its derived steps in `derived:`.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

dc builds this package and claims `ST0091/01` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0091/01`, once the vendor sweep has brought the new core into Intent's tree. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What moves

dc's inventory, measured at 7ff46b458; line references are to that commit. dc read it again on 2026-11-10 at 9ff4b3e9c, against the vendored devbin 0.1.20 core (`refs/bank/dc/st0091/wp01-inventory-v2.md`, which holds the first inventory whole and dc's re-read at file and line), and vc's rulings on that read are the section below.

- `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release` (1524 lines) goes. Its pre-flight (:534) goes to the core's pre-flight and its version stamp (sidecar sync, :942) to the core's stamp. Its confirmation (:245), tag (:1418), push to both remotes (:1459, :1461) and GitHub release (:1468-1505) go to the core's one yes before anything runs, the tag on green, the push and the release object.
- `release.verbs` gains `cut`.
- `derived:` carries the schema-face bless (:1066), the lock refresh, the stamp CLI (:1188), `agents sync` (:1200), `claude upgrade --apply` (:1250) and `sync --to-disk` (:1289). Each is a project command that prints on stdout the paths it wrote and nothing else, because the core takes every stdout line of a derived command into the set of paths the release owns.
- `release.gates` declares Intent's own checks, which stay Intent's: the bats suite (:725); the cargo gate (:767-847), with issue 0481's one re-run of intentd's load-sensitive family (:827) moving into Intent's own gate command, because the core re-runs nothing and a red local leg stops the cut; the ST0056 contract and reference checks (:638, :659), which ST0084 later moves; the embedded-source-commit check `macos publish` makes today (`cmd/macos` :1405, against the string at `native/rust/crates/intentd/src/main.rs:75`), keyed on the release commit; and the pair build at the release commit (`pair_at_tag`, :290), held to macOS, which keeps issue 0518's currency verdict green on the release push. A sealed green for a commit and platform is not run again (Devbin D57).
- The refusal of a live intentd (:704) runs at the core's pre-flight, before the confirmation and before anything is stamped, and the dry run reaches it. The 0.1.20 core has no seam there for a project's own check, so vc asked devbin-vc for one on 2026-11-10, and the check's wiring waits for it.
- `tests/unit/release_script.bats` and `release_sidecars.bats` follow what they test.

## Rulings on dc's re-inventory

vc's, on 2026-11-10, under hv's pen, each checked in the vendored source and each open to hv's reversal. The inventory is `refs/bank/dc/st0091/wp01-inventory-v2.md`: section C holds the findings, and section E dc's re-read at file and line.

- **The live-intentd refusal (C1).** It belongs at the core's pre-flight, through a declared list of `bin/devbin <words>` lines that a dry run and a cut both run. The 0.1.20 core has no such list, and vc asked devbin-vc for it. dc builds the check now as one project verb that writes nothing, and wires it when the seam exists. Three ways that need no devbin change are refused. A project `release` handler shadows every release verb, `release gates` on a remote leg included. A refusal in the first derived step comes after the confirmation and after `version set`, and the dry run passes where the cut refuses. A notes provider's `state` is also read by `release status`, `release check` and the stamp's read-back, so it would refuse those while intentd runs. If devbin-vc declines, which cost to pay is hv's to say.
- **What the dry run names (C2).** The core's dry run names every leg and gives a count of derived commands, and `bin/devbin release check` names every derived command and gate. AC-01.1 is reworded to that.
- **The candidate's trigger (C4).** `tests.yml` fires on a push to main and on tags, so the core's pre-flight refuses a cut and a dry run until the workflows fire on `candidate/` refs. `ci.query: -` is not used to get past it. WP-04's trigger change is built first and banked as the train's first unit.
- **The pair build (C8).** It is a gate and not a derived step, because a derived step runs before the release commit exists and the pair must embed that commit. It is held to macOS by `platforms:` on an option of a gate that runs its command's `all`, which the core honours and whose pre-flight refuses an option active on no leg. That is vc's source read, and dc drives it.
- **Size (C14).** WP-01 is M.
- **Where a check lives.** A check that judges the tree as it stands before the stamp, and writes nothing, belongs at the pre-flight seam: the live intentd, and the schema faces carrying the current version. A check whose truth depends on the release commit is a gate: reference currency, the embedded source commit, the suites and the pair. Each check has one home, and dc's design shows the split.
- **Built this way until hv rules.** `release.remotes` is declared as `local` and `upstream`, so the third remote takes nothing (C3). The core's release commit message, `release: <tag>` alone, stands (C10).
- **Forced by the core (C9).** Its formula step refuses a lightweight tag, so Intent's release tags are annotated from 3.3.0. Intent's own readers of a tag peel it already, and dc's bank says which it checked.

## The judge

One heavy run on the bank's tip, booked through devbin-vc's desk: the whole bats tree and the whole cargo suites, because hook and scanner arms read shell and config files; `intent critic shell --files` on each changed shell file; `prettier --check` on each changed `.md`; `bin/int precommit` over the staged tree; and the core's dry run of Intent's cut, read for every derived step, gate and leg. dc mints this package's AT rows with its bank, and each arm carries its AT id from the start. dc may bank WP-01 to WP-04 as one train, judged in one run and landed in order.

wps.title: kovacs runs as the cut's remote leg, and prepush keeps only its push gates
wps.objective: kovacs runs Intent's declared gates at the release commit as a `release.legs` leg inside the cut, instead of an order run by hand before it. `bin/.devbin/preflight-linux.sh` and `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/preflight.lib` are gone, and `bin/int prepush` keeps its push gates but neither requires a kovacs summary nor clones and builds the workspace.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

dc builds this package and claims `ST0091/02` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0091/02`, once the vendor sweep has brought in the core's remote-leg runner (Devbin WP05). vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What moves

dc's inventory, measured at 7ff46b458; line references are to that commit.

- `release.legs` names kovacs (Devbin D62): the core pushes the release commit to a scratch bare repo on kovacs, runs Intent's declared gates in a worktree there and copies the seal back. kovacs carries what those gates need, the tools `preflight-linux.sh` checks for today.
- `bin/.devbin/preflight-linux.sh` (235 lines) and `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/preflight.lib` (40) go.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/prepush` loses its Linux preflight cover (:204-265, :475) and its clone-and-build (:508-509). Its frozen-remote list (:140), which the driver checks at :594, stays as a push gate, and so do its other push checks.
- The candidate goes to `upstream` only, the remote found by its URL, and `local` receives main and the tag on green. That is the core's (Devbin WP02b, with cc), and Intent's part is its config.
- The preflight arms of `tests/unit/prepush_push_range.bats` (:440-576) follow what they test.

## The judge

As WP-01's.

wps.title: The tap and the macOS assets publish through the built-ins, with prepare as a shadow
wps.objective: The built-in formula writes Intent's tap and the built-in `macos publish` uploads its macOS assets, both under the cut's yes. `bin/.devbin/cmd/brew` keeps Intent's own smoke and nothing else, and the cut runs that smoke as an `after:` command. `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` keeps no publish, and its `prepare` stays as a shadow that writes the stage's commit record the built-in publish requires.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

dc builds this package and claims `ST0091/03` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0091/03`, once the vendor sweep has brought in the core's formula under the yes (Devbin WP08) and its macOS stage (Devbin WP06), both of which devbin 0.1.20 carries as vendored. vc judges it and claims nothing.

## What moves

dc's inventory, measured at 7ff46b458; line references are to that commit.

- `bin/.devbin/cmd/brew` (669 lines) loses its render and its publish to the built-in `formula` (the vendored `lib/cmd/formula`), which writes Intent's formula and cask in assets mode under the cut's yes and fills each asset's sum from the release's sums file. That fill is what stands for issue 0634's cask sha256 check: no sum is kept by hand, and none is computed on this machine.
- `cmd/brew` keeps its smoke (`cmd_smoke`, :265, about half the file). The core carries none: devbin-vc measured on 2026-11-10 that the smoke its ruling of 2026-10-31 named was never built. The cut runs Intent's as an `after:` command, where it reports after publication and gates nothing, as it does today after `brew publish`.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/brew.lib` (812) keeps only what the smoke reads, or goes if the smoke reads nothing from it, and dc's bank says which. `cmd/macos` sources `brew.lib` (:76), and that line follows what is left of it.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` (2349 lines) loses its publish half (`cmd_publish`, :1245-1536) to the built-in `macos publish`. Its `prepare` (:1192) stays as a shadow until the built-in stages more than one app, and writes `<stage>/commit`, HEAD's full sha, because the built-in publish refuses a stage without one (Devbin WP06a's note). Today neither `cmd/macos` nor the vendored `lib/cmd/macos` writes that file: the stage (:835) records `commit:` in `target/dist-provenance.txt` (:893) instead.
- `tests/unit/brew_formula.bats` and `macos_release_assets.bats` follow what they test.

## The judge

As WP-01's.

wps.title: The workflows fire on the candidate, and the docs describe the cut as built
wps.objective: `tests.yml`, `rust.yml` and `linux-release.yml` fire on `candidate/` refs and not on tags (Devbin D64), so every leg, the macOS legs included, is green on the commit that ships before it is tagged. The five commands run by hand after the tag stop, and `intent/docs/releasing.md` and `.github/workflows/README.md` describe the cut as built.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

dc builds this package and claims `ST0091/04` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0091/04`, once the vendor sweep has brought in the core's candidate push (Devbin WP02b) and its attach keyed on the release commit (Devbin WP07). vc judges it and claims nothing. hv fires the first cut through the core in hv's own terminal, and vc records it on AC-04.3; Devbin's WP06 and WP07 are accepted at that cut (Devbin D66).

## What moves

dc's inventory, measured at 7ff46b458; line references are to that commit.

- `tests.yml` (:8) and `rust.yml` (:31) lose their tag triggers and fire on `candidate/` refs, the macOS legs included, which today run only on a tag or a dispatch. `linux-release.yml` (:22-25) fires on `candidate/` instead of tags, and the attach reads its run by the release commit's sha (`bin/.devbin/config.yaml` :371-372 names the workflow).
- The five commands run by hand after the tag stop: `bin/int macos prepare`, `bin/int macos publish`, `bin/devbin release attach vX.Y.Z`, `bin/int brew publish` and `bin/int brew smoke --reinstall` (`intent/docs/releasing.md` :119). They are the item parked for hv in `intent/wip.md`, "Intent's cut wants one driver", which this package retires.
- `intent/docs/releasing.md` (:13, :101-140) describes the one command, and stops promising a dry run that runs the pre-flight gates for real: the core's dry run predicts and runs no gate (Devbin D63). `.github/workflows/README.md` (:55-57) follows; its linux-release section still says dispatch-only, though the workflow has fired on tags since 9f4994a1c.

## The judge

As WP-01's, with `bin/devbin release check` run on the bank's tree.

criteria.text: `bin/devbin release` cuts Intent through devbin's core: the schema bless, the lock refresh, `agents sync`, `claude upgrade --apply` and `sync --to-disk` run as `derived:` steps, `bin/devbin release check` names every derived step and gate, the dry run names every leg and runs no derived step and no gate, and `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release` is gone.

Intent's own checks run as declared `release.gates`: the bats suite, the cargo gate with issue 0481's daemon-family re-run inside Intent's own gate command, the ST0056 contract and reference checks, the embedded-source-commit check keyed on the release commit, and, on macOS alone, the pair build at the release commit; a sealed green for the release commit on this platform is not run again.
The cut and its dry run refuse while an intentd is live, before anything is stamped, and the remedy says how to stop the daemon.
The pair the cut builds at the release commit passes issue 0518's currency verdict when the release push runs.
kovacs runs Intent's declared gates at the release commit as a `release.legs` leg inside the cut, and `bin/.devbin/preflight-linux.sh` and `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/preflight.lib` are gone.
`bin/int prepush` keeps its frozen-remote refusal, and a push neither requires a kovacs summary nor clones and builds the workspace.

The built-in formula writes Intent's formula and cask in assets mode under the cut's yes, each asset's sum filled from the release's sums file, which stands for issue 0634's cask sha256 check; Intent's own brew smoke runs as an `after:` command under the same yes, where it reports after publication and gates nothing; and `bin/.devbin/cmd/brew` keeps the smoke and nothing else, with no render or publish code left in it or in `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/brew.lib`.
The built-in `macos publish` publishes the stage Intent's `macos prepare` makes, that stage carries `<stage>/commit` with HEAD's full sha, and `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` carries no publish.

The service block in Intent's formula template points log_path and error_log_path at D19's intentd.log and intentd.err.log under the user's state dir, the files intent daemon logs reads, and its comment says intentd writes every line to stdout or stderr and names where each goes (issue 0667, ruled by hv on 2026-10-31).
`tests.yml`, `rust.yml` and `linux-release.yml` fire on `candidate/` refs and not on tags, the macOS legs included, and `bin/devbin release check` passes on Intent's tree.

`intent/docs/releasing.md` and `.github/workflows/README.md` describe the cut as built: one command from the yes to the tap with no step between them run by hand, a dry run that predicts and runs no gate, then `brew upgrade` and `intent use brew` on each machine.
hv cuts Intent's first release through the core with no hand step between the yes and the tap, and vc records that cut's RELEASE seal clock lines against the 3.2.8 baseline.

tests.note: Minted by dc with the train's first bank, refs/bank/dc/st0091/wp04-trigger-v1 (blob ee3409fcdced, patch-id 2c4e9bc3ab35, base 991e92946). It stays to-write until the train lands: the file is in the bank and not yet on main, and `intent at red` refuses a row whose cited file is absent, since that would be a live absent_at finding. The judge of the train's tip sets its verdict. Its three tests: a push of the cut's candidate starts release.ci.workflow as committed at HEAD, asked of devbin's own reader (`ci-state --fires`); no tag push starts tests.yml, rust.yml or linux-release.yml; and a candidate's run carries the macOS leg and rust.yml's job, each keyed on the candidate prefix config names. Each test reads the candidate template from config, never a literal. Each red was driven, and each is the base's own line restored: test 1 with HEAD at 991e92946, whose committed tests.yml admits no candidate; test 2 with linux-release.yml's base L25, `tags: ["v[0-9]*"]`, back under push; test 3 with tests.yml's base L292, test-macos's tag condition, back. AC-04.1's release-check half is judged at the tip, once WP-01 offers cut.
